answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by giving each established identity a small endorsement budget that refills slowly, like a plume spreading only so far each epoch. A newcomer gains weight only when established agents spend budget vouching for it, and a vouch that later proves fake burns the voucher's budget too. A fake swarm is then no relic of cheap signups: each clone needs scarce vouches from accounts that took months to earn standing, so the attacker must either age hundreds of accounts in public or corrupt real ones, and every failed clone destroys the ledge of trust it climbed in on.
